summary: Turns your development process into YAML workflows that coding agents like Claude Code and Codex follow the same way every time.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Archon is a workflow engine for AI coding. You describe how work should get done as a YAML graph of steps: agents handle judgment (planning, implementing), scripts handle checks (like running tests until they pass), and approval gates pause for your decisions. Archon runs Claude Code, Codex and Pi through their own CLIs with the accounts you already have. A bundled software pack takes an issue all the way to a merged pull request, and every run keeps an event log, transcript and cost record in your own database.
sixtySeconds.problem: Ask a coding agent to fix something and it may skip the plan, forget tests or ignore your PR template. Archon makes the process fixed and repeatable, so you only step in for real decisions.
whoFor: Developers who rely on Claude Code or Codex
Teams that want consistent agent output
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it to make agent coding runs deterministic with your own steps, checks and approval gates, self-hosted.
requirements: A git repository to run workflows in

overview: Install Claude Code or Codex first, then install Archon with the script for your OS or with Homebrew; the installer asks which providers to add.
In any git repo, list workflows with archon workflow list and start one with archon workflow run.
Follow runs and answer their questions in the web console (archon serve) or the terminal. MIT licensed; it stores data in SQLite by default.
